# Claude Code Interface Contract

<!-- GENERATED from src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/claude.contract.ts by scripts/generate-contract-docs.mjs — do not edit. Run `npm run contract:docs`. -->

Every external interface of Claude Code that Cinna relies on, one entry each: what the tool must do, which Cinna code depends on it, and what the user loses when it stops. **Verified against Claude Code CLI 2.1.276 with `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.76.0** — the versions pinned in `src/shared/runtimePins.ts`.

Each entry has exactly one test, titled with its id, in [`claude.contract.test.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/claude.contract.test.ts). They run the real pinned binary and the real adapter over stdio against a loopback fake provider — no login, no provider request — with `npm run test:contract` (`make contract ENGINE=claude` installs the binary first). They are not part of `npm test`.

The raw shapes a run observes are compared with the committed [`claude-2.1.276.json`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/snapshots/claude-2.1.276.json), and a difference fails the run; `make contract-snapshot ENGINE=claude` rewrites it once a change is understood. To evaluate a new release, `make contract-next ENGINE=claude VERSION=<x.y.z>` runs the same tests against that version without changing the pin; red entries name their owners below, and the run prints the diff between the pinned snapshot and the candidate's (written to a temp path, never into the tree) — that diff is what changed.

Hand-written evidence and reasoning stay in [The ACP Engine Contract](../acp_contract.md) and [The Claude Engine Contract](../claude_contract.md); this file is only the index of what is checked.

**Flow step** names the step of the Level 2 whole flow that exercises the entry — **A** plain chat on the Default runtime, then its AI title; **B** a specialist @-added mid-chat, called through Cinna’s MCP server; **C** continuity: a later turn remembers the first; **D** a specialist attached before the first turn. A dash means no step does, and the note says why. For Claude Code only the billed variant walks them: `make live-flow ENGINE=claude` (the user’s real login, manual). The no-billing `e2e/specs/runtime-flow.spec.ts` covers Codex alone — Cinna strips `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and the key variables from every Claude child by design, so an app-spawned session cannot be sent to a fake provider without a new production seam.

An entry marked **Live only** cannot be exercised against a fake provider — it needs a real login or the vendor’s servers. Its test is skipped, never faked, and the entry says why; it is checked by the live flow instead.

## Launch & env

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude.launch.version-output` | CLI: `--version` | Prints exactly `<version> (Claude Code)` on stdout and exits 0. | [`binaryResolver.ts`](../../../../src/main/engine/binaryResolver.ts) `CLAUDE_SPEC` | The managed install is discarded as the wrong version, and an up-to-date install of the user’s own is never reused. | **A** — the live flow asserts the resolved binary reports the pinned version |
| `claude.launch.executable` | env var: `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` | The adapter runs the executable this variable names, not the `claude` its own SDK dependency bundles. | [`acpLaunchers.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpLaunchers.ts) `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` | Sessions run on an unpinned Claude Code — or none at all in the packaged app, which excludes the bundled copy. | **A** |
| `claude.launch.child-env` | env var: `PATH / HOME / USER` | A session starts and completes a turn on the narrowed child environment alone: PATH, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL and HOME, plus what the launcher adds. | [`claudeEnv.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/claudeEnv.ts) `buildClaudeEnv` | Every Claude turn fails at start, or runs with variables the desktop meant to withhold. | **A** |
| `claude.launch.autoupdater-disabled` | env var: `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` | **Live only.** With `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` the CLI’s background updater never runs: a Cinna-spawned process does not download a newer Claude Code or retarget `~/.local/bin/claude`. *Why not here:* Nothing differs in a contract run. Probed 2026-09-18 on 2.1.276 behind the egress trap: `claude update` contacts `downloads.claude.ai` with or without the variable (it governs the *background* updater, not the command), and a non-interactive session never checks for an update either way — the updater belongs to the long-lived interactive process, under a real install layout. | [`claudeEnv.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/claudeEnv.ts) `buildClaudeEnv`<br>[`claudeEnv.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/claudeEnv.ts) `AUTOUPDATER_ENV` | A desktop session silently moves the user’s own `claude` to another version, and a pooled adapter’s next spawn runs a version that never passed the pin gate. | — every step runs with the variable set, but none observes the updater; walked by hand on a long session |

## Auth

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude.auth.status-json` | CLI: `auth status` | Prints a JSON object with a boolean `loggedIn` and a string `authMethod`; with no login it reports `loggedIn: false`, `authMethod: "none"`. `orgId`/`orgName`, when present, are extra keys. | [`claudeAuth.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/claudeAuth.ts) `parseClaudeAuthStatus`<br>[`claudeAuth.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/claudeAuth.ts) `probeClaudeAuth` | Readiness cannot tell a logged-out install from a working one: the panel stops naming the login, and a logged-out agent fails at its first turn instead of being told to log in. | **A** — the login probe before the first turn |
| `claude.auth.login-follows-home` | file: `HOME (Keychain / ~/.claude)` | **Live only.** A second Claude Code binary, run with the user’s real HOME and USER, reports the same subscription login as their own install, with no Keychain prompt. *Why not here:* Needs the user’s real subscription login and Keychain entry; an isolated HOME has neither. Verified by hand 2026-09-18 (2.1.266 from node_modules reported the 2.1.276 install’s Max login). | [`index.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/index.ts) `claudeAuthProbe`<br>[`claudeEnv.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/claudeEnv.ts) `buildClaudeEnv` | The managed CLI is logged out on a machine whose user is logged in: every Claude agent stops until they log in a second time. | **A** — live flow only: the first turn on the resolved binary answers on the user’s own login |

## Provider traffic

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude.provider.base-url` | env var: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Every Messages request goes to `POST <base>/v1/messages` with the given key as `x-api-key`. **This is what the whole contract stands on**: red here means no other entry was really checked. | [`claudeHarness.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/claudeHarness.ts) `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Nothing in the product — Cinna strips these variables from a real session. The contract run would silently stop being hermetic. | — test infrastructure |
| `claude.provider.auxiliary-request` | provider request: `session title` | The CLI’s only request of its own is a **session title**: system prompt opening "You are naming a coding…", the session’s text inside `<session>…</session>`, no tools, on the conversation’s model. It is sent beside the first prompt — carrying the user’s first message — and again after turns. No compaction or other request appears in a short session. | [`claudeHarness.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/claudeHarness.ts) `isClaudeTitleRequest` | Characterised, not depended on: a user’s first message is sent a second time, on their subscription, for a title Cinna does not show. A new kind of request appearing here is a cost and privacy change worth a line in the release notes. | **A** — sent beside the first turn; the live flow cannot observe it |
| `claude.provider.no-real-egress` | network: `api.anthropic.com` | With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set the CLI **still tries `api.anthropic.com`** on its own. Every attempt the CLI routed through `HTTPS_PROXY` was to `api.anthropic.com:443` and was refused before TLS; the dummy key never left the loopback endpoint. The trap sees proxy-honouring traffic only — it is a record of what the CLI sends through its HTTP stack, not a firewall. | [`claudeHarness.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/contracts/claudeHarness.ts) `startEgressTrap` | A contract run would make real requests to the vendor. A new host appearing here is a new place the CLI sends something. | — test infrastructure |

## Limits

| Id | Surface | Expectation | Owners | Feature at risk | Flow step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude.limits.rate-limit-kind` | ACP field: `error.data.errorKind` | A provider 429 (`rate_limit_error`) fails the prompt with a JSON-RPC error whose `data.errorKind` is `"rate_limit"`. | [`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `errorKind`<br>[`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `rate_limit` | A rate-limited conductor is reported as a generic failure and retried at once, instead of pausing until the limit lifts. | — no step produces a 429 |
| `claude.limits.subscription-limit` | ACP field: `error.data.errorKind (subscription)` | **Live only.** Reaching a **subscription** usage limit is reported with the same `errorKind: "rate_limit"` as an API 429. *Why not here:* A subscription limit is produced by the vendor’s servers for a logged-in account; a fake endpoint can only return an API-key 429, which `claude.limits.rate-limit-kind` covers. | [`acpDriver.ts`](../../../../src/main/agents/drivers/acp/acpDriver.ts) `rate_limit` | A Max or Pro user who runs out of quota sees a raw error and an immediate retry loop. | — live, and not reproducible on demand |
